result.title: TADP: Dual-Branch Temporally Adaptive Differential Privacy for Expression-Aware Video Anonymization
result.summary: We present TADP, a temporally adaptive differential privacy (DP) framework for inference-time privacy-preserving video generation under fixed-length clip-replacement adjacency. TADP uses a dual-branch design to extract identity and expression representations, clips and privatizes both branches with temporally adaptive Gaussian mechanisms whose noise scales depend only on preceding privatized releases within the same clip and are bounded below by history-uniform calibrated minima, and accounts for their joint release via adaptive Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) composition. The clip-level RDP guarantee is converted to $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differential privacy, while soft quantization and subsequent temporal processing are applied only after privatization as DP post-processing. Experiments on facial expression datasets show reduced identity leakage under evaluated attacks, usable perceptual quality and temporal stability, and high facial expression recognition utility relative to the evaluated privacy-preserving baselines. TADP formally satisfies clip-level DP and empirically provides a favorable privacy--utility trade-off under the evaluated threat models and datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TADP，用双分支分别提取身份与表情表示，在推理期对两分支施加时间自适应高斯噪声并做 RDP 组合，实现视频人脸匿名化，同时保留可用的表情识别效用与时间稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式分离任务必要的表情信息与应抑制的身份信息，对 latent 表示加噪并以下游识别效用衡量信息保留」的思路，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与信息坍缩的度量方式，但该文不涉及推理状态生成。
